title: Help in goodness
hookLine: help one another in righteousness and mindfulness, not in sin (5:2)
tomorrow: Food of the People of the Book

lines: A FRIEND CALLS LATE AT NIGHT.
cards: A friend calls late at night. I need a favor. Can you tell my boss I was with you yesterday?
Can you lend me money, for the thing you suspect it's for again? Can you help me get back at my ex? Loyalty pulls one way.
Something else pulls the other. The second verse of al-Ma'idah gives a short rule for it, and a hadith turns that rule into something surprising.

teach.b: Verse 2 begins with the pilgrimage: its sacred months, its offerings, the pilgrims on their way.
It warns the believers not to let resentment toward the people who once blocked them from the Sacred Mosque push them into aggression.
Then, in Pickthall's words: "Help ye one another unto righteousness and pious duty. Help not one another unto sin and transgression." Two Arabic words carry it.

Birr, righteousness, a wide, warm word for goodness, the same word used for kindness to parents. And taqwa, mindfulness of God, the awareness that keeps you careful. So the verse doesn't say help your friends.
It says help with good. The direction matters more than the person. A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari makes it vivid.

teach.h: HELP THE OPPRESSOR BY STOPPING HIM
teach.b: The Prophet ﷺ said: help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed. The companions were puzzled. Helping the oppressed, they understood.
But how do we help him if he's the oppressor? The Prophet answered: by stopping him. That's help, too.

Sometimes the loyal answer to the late-night call is no, and then a better offer: I won't lie to your boss, but I'll help you talk to him. I won't lend you that money, but I'll drive you to the meeting.
Another hadith, in Sahih Muslim, says whoever points someone to good gets a reward like the one who does it.

teach.h: HELP YE ONE ANOTHER UNTO RIGHTEOUSNESS.
teach.b: So helping in goodness isn't only refusing. It's also cheering, driving, lending, showing the way.

how: Muslim teachers often cite 5:2 for mutual aid, volunteering and charitable cooperation, and for refusing help in wrongdoing, even to friends.

o: a reward paid back for a favor
a vow of loyalty to your friends

games.q: help in goodness — tap the pairs.

s: 5:2 says help your friends, whatever they ask
it says help in righteousness and mindfulness, never in sin.
the Prophet said to help an oppressor
the verse lets old resentment justify aggression
it warns not to let hatred of those who blocked the pilgrims push you to transgress.

games.q: the Prophet says: help your brother, whether oppressor or oppressed. the companions ask how you help an oppressor. what does he answer?
games.why: by stopping him from oppressing. holding someone back from wrong is a form of help (Sahih al-Bukhari).

practice: Think of someone trying to do something good right now: study, get healthy, quit something, care for a parent.
Picture what they're up against, and one concrete help you could give, not advice but help: a ride, an hour, a meal, a message at the right moment.

wordCard.voice: Birr, a wide, warm word for goodness. Help one another in it and in taqwa, mindfulness of God, never in sin and aggression, from 5:2. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: and help one another in righteousness and mindfulness (5:2).

carryVoice: Your line: help in good only. The direction matters more than the person. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: Help ye one another unto righteousness and pious duty. Help not one another unto sin and transgression.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2444 (help your brother, oppressor or oppressed)
